newsitem.title: USA: US March income data suggest moderate growth in Q2.
newsitem.headline: US March income data suggest moderate growth in Q2.

text.p: A 0.6 percent rise in the March personal income data combined with a slight increase in the savings rate suggest the U.S. economy might be growing at a more moderate pace in the second quarter, analysts said.

"The first quarter was very strong. It's not likely that we're going to be that strong in the second quarter, particularly with the savings rate starting to tick up a little bit," said Gary Thayer, senior economist at A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc.
"That suggests to me that we might see more moderate growth here in the second quarter," Thayer added.

Thayer was referring to a red hot 5.6 percent growth measured by the U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the first quarter of 1997. The U.S. savings rate rose to 5.3 percent in March against 5.2 percent in February.
The income data failed to shake financial markets as participants continued to brace for the release of the April payrolls report on Friday.
Analysts said the data are seen as key for the Federal Reserve.

"I think the Fed will be looking very carefully at the next set of numbers that come out, and any indication that the economy is not slowing down probably will tend to push them towards another (rate) increase in the May meeting," said Kathryn Kobe from Joel Popkin & Co.
"So the employment tomorrow is going to be an important one," she added.

The payroll data will be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted down 2/32 shortly after the personal income data were released. The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee will meet again on May 20.
